newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks head higher in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks head higher in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks inched higher in Thursday morning trade, buoyed by buying in laggards and second line stocks.
The Hang Seng index was up 64 points at 13,498. Turnover was HK$1.75 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
"No one is willing to retreat from the market any time soon. Everyone wants to stay in," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
However, an overnight decline on Wall Street kept some investors on the sidelines, some analysts said.

"It seems that the U.S. market is under consolidation so some people will tend to stay on the sidelines or are looking for opportunities in second liners," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
Dow industrials fell 19.75 points to 6,422.94 on Wednesday.
Mak said investors were choosing to rotate, with selected utilities moving ahead. China Light rose HK$0.20 to HK$34.40 and Hongkong Electric gained HK$1.00 to HK$27.65.
Meanwhile some of the blue chips took a breather. New World Development was off HK$0.25 at HK$51.00. Henderson Land was unchanged at HK$78.50.
"For most of the blue chips, the gains are quite impressive so far this year so blue chips are taking a break," said Chia.
He said Friday's release of the U.S. November payrolls report was also making some investors cautious.

Wheelock, which announced a 48 percent fall in interim net profit on Wednesday, was down HK$0.15 at HK$21.55. Analysts said the results were slightly disappointing but expected a better performance in the second half due to higher property sales.

Shares in China Elegance rose HK$0.15 to HK$4.375. The company said it plans to issue 40 million new shares to Mansyong International Development Ltd at HK$3.95 per share, raising net proceeds of about HK$156 million.

Shares in Cathay Pacific were down HK$0.05 at HK$12.45. The Hong Kong flag carrier said on Thursday it aims to raise air ticket prices by three percent in mid-December following approval by the Civil Aviation Department (CAD) for such a move.
